response: The insertion allele (I allele) of the ACE gene I/D polymorphism has been associated with various conditions, but its direct link to insulin resistance as a candidate gene is not strongly established. However, some studies suggest that the ACE gene I/D polymorphism may influence insulin sensitivity indirectly through its effects on the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), which can impact vascular function and potentially contribute to metabolic syndrome components, including insulin resistance. Nonetheless, the relationship between the ACE gene I/D polymorphism and insulin resistance is complex and may be influenced by other genetic and environmental factors.
